draft.title: Types of business ownership
card: Sole trader
One person owns the business. The law does not treat the owner and the business as separate, so the owner is personally liable for all its debts. Profit is taxed as the owner's own income.
Partnership

Two or more people own the business and share its profit as agreed. Partners are personally liable for the business debts. The partnership does not pay income tax itself: each partner pays tax on their share of the profit.
Company

A company is a separate legal entity owned by shareholders. Shareholders are usually liable only for any amount unpaid on their shares, not for the company's debts. The company pays tax on its own profit.
Liable means legally responsible. If a business with personally liable owners cannot pay its debts, the owners' own assets, such as a car or savings, may be used to pay them.
draft.remember: Sole traders and partners are personally liable for debts. A company is a separate entity that pays its own tax.

a.q: Priya owns a bakery as a sole trader, and it cannot pay a supplier. What can the supplier do about the debt?
opts: Claim against Priya's own assets as well as the bakery's
Claim only against the bakery's own assets
Claim against the bakery's customers
Claim against the tax office
a.why: A sole trader and the business are not separate in law, so Priya is personally liable. The supplier can seek payment from her own assets too. Claiming only against the bakery's assets fits a company, not a sole trader.
a.clue: Does the law treat Priya and her bakery as separate?

b.q: Tom and Aisha run a Geelong cycle shop as a partnership, and the shop makes a profit. Which statement about tax and debts is correct?
opts: Each pays tax on their share, and both are liable for debts
The shop pays tax, and both are liable for debts
Each pays tax on their share, and neither is liable for debts
The shop pays tax, and neither is liable for debts
b.why: A partnership does not pay income tax itself, so Tom and Aisha each pay tax on their share of the profit. Partners are also personally liable for the debts. The shop paying its own tax describes a company, which is a separate entity.
b.clue: A partnership is not a separate legal entity.
